gemma_4_31b.narrative:
I am initiating the exploration phase by registering a comprehensive set of hypotheses based on established clinical oncology knowledge and exploratory markers. 

First, I am testing the efficacy of targeted therapies in their biomarker-defined populations: Sotorasib for KRAS G12C, Osimertinib for EGFR mutations, and Olaparib for BRCA2 mutations. I expect these to show a positive effect on progression-free survival (PFS).

Second, I am evaluating Pembrolizumab efficacy in patients with high PD-L1 expression (TPS >= 50%) and high tumor mutational burden (TMB), as these are recognized predictors of response to PD-1 inhibition.

Third, I am registering several known negative prognostic indicators: high Neutrophil-to-Lymphocyte Ratio (NLR >= 3), poor performance status (ECOG PS >= 2), the presence of brain metastases, low albumin (<= 3.5 g/dL), and high C-Reactive Protein (CRP >= 10 mg/L). I expect these to be associated with shorter PFS.

Finally, I am including exploratory analyses for Research Markers D, E, and F to determine if they have any association with PFS, with no prior expectation of direction.

Plausible alternatives for the targeted/immunotherapy claims include the possibility that the biomarkers are not predictive in this specific cohort or that resistance mechanisms override the benefit. For prognostic markers, the observed effects might be confounded by overall disease stage or other comorbidities.

qwen_3_8_27b.narrative:
This is the first iteration with no prior claims or evidence in the ledger. Both peer drafts are identical, proposing 10 hypotheses across three tiers: (1) main treatment effects for pembrolizumab, sotorasib, osimertinib, and olaparib; (2) four biomarker-by-treatment interactions (PD-L1×pembrolizumab, KRAS G12C×sotorasib, EGFR×osimertinib, TMB×pembrolizumab); and (3) two prognostic factors (NLR≥3, ECOG PS≥2). I adopt all 10 peer proposals without modification because they are scientifically well-motivated and cover the core questions. I add four additional hypotheses to close critical gaps:

(1) Olaparib×BRCA2 interaction: This is the most important omission. Olaparib is a PARP inhibitor whose mechanism of action is synthetic lethality in BRCA-mutant tumors. BRCA2 mutation prevalence is ~3% (≈1,493 patients), and olaparib is administered to ~30% of the cohort, yielding roughly 450 exposed and 1,040 comparator patients in the BRCA2+ subgroup—well above the 20-observation minimum. The interaction contrast (effect in BRCA2+ minus effect in BRCA2−) is anticipated to be positive, meaning olaparib should confer a larger PFS benefit in BRCA2-mutant patients.

(2) STK11×pembrolizumab interaction: STK11 (LKB1) loss is a well-established mechanism of primary resistance to PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors in NSCLC. STK11 mutation prevalence is ~15% (≈7,452 patients), and with pembrolizumab at ~50%, the subgroup has ~3,700 patients. I anticipate a negative interaction: pembrolizumab's PFS benefit should be attenuated in STK11-mutant patients relative to STK11-wild-type patients. Direction is −1 because the interaction contrast (subgroup effect minus complement effect) is expected to be negative.

(3) Albumin ≤ 3.5 g/dL: Hypoalbuminemia is a well-known negative prognostic marker in cancer, reflecting malnutrition, systemic inflammation, and hepatic dysfunction. Prevalence is ~31% (≈15,400 patients). I anticipate a negative mean difference (lower PFS in the hypoalbuminemic group).

(4) CRP ≥ 10 mg/L: Elevated C-reactive protein is a marker of systemic inflammation and is associated with worse outcomes in multiple cancer types. Prevalence is ~16% (≈7,933 patients). I anticipate a negative mean difference.

All 14 proposals are registered as unresolved with active investigation since no evidence exists yet. The clinical significance threshold is 10% relative difference on log PFS (mean ≈ 2.06), corresponding to approximately 0.21 log-months. For main treatment effects, I anticipate positive directions; for the four biomarker-matched interactions (PD-L1, KRAS G12C, EGFR, TMB, BRCA2), I anticipate positive directions; for STK11×pembrolizumab, I anticipate a negative direction; and for the three prognostic factors (NLR, ECOG PS, albumin, CRP), I anticipate negative directions. Next iteration will analyze these 14 hypotheses and then consider research signatures A/B/C, research markers D/E/F, additional prognostic markers (LDH, weight loss, hemoglobin), and ALK fusion as a prognostic or treatment-interaction variable.
